edges.description: Failure of midline callosal axon crossing results in complete agenesis of the corpus callosum.
Partial failure of commissural axon guidance produces corpus callosum hypoplasia.
Defective long-tract axon guidance and decussation cause corticospinal tract hypoplasia.
Corticospinal tract maldevelopment causes congenital and progressive lower-limb spastic paraplegia.
Corticospinal tract dysfunction and lower-extremity spasticity manifest as a shuffling gait.
Callosal maldevelopment and abnormal cortical connectivity are associated with intellectual disability across the L1 spectrum.
Commissural and cortical network dysgenesis is associated with delayed or impaired speech (aphasia) in the MASA spectrum.
Narrowing or obstruction of the cerebral aqueduct of Sylvius manifests as aqueductal stenosis.
Impaired cerebrospinal fluid outflow through the stenotic aqueduct causes cerebral ventricular dilation (ventriculomegaly).
Progressive cerebrospinal fluid accumulation upstream of aqueductal obstruction produces congenital hydrocephalus.
Severe congenital hydrocephalus and aqueductal stenosis in HSAS are associated with severe intellectual disability.

nodes.description: Loss-of-function or hypomorphic variants in L1CAM impair the function of the L1 cell adhesion molecule, a single-pass transmembrane glycoprotein of the immunoglobulin superfamily expressed in neurons and Schwann cells. L1 is essential for nervous system development, mediating cell adhesion, signaling, and membrane trafficking. Mutations are distributed across the functional protein domains; the precise mechanisms by which they cause loss of L1 function are incompletely understood.

nodes.description: L1 normally promotes neurite outgrowth, axon guidance/pathfinding, and neuronal migration. A 2023 mechanistic study showed that the L1-70 fragment binds LC3 (an autophagy-related protein) via an extracellular LC3-interacting region (LIR) motif in the fourth fibronectin type III domain, and that this interaction is required for L1-mediated neurite outgrowth and neuronal survival, linking L1CAM processing to autophagy-related machinery. Loss of L1 function therefore impairs the formation of major axon tracts.
